Task (generic)

General Concept: A Task in BPMN is a generic activity representing a unit of work. It can be specialized into Service Task, User Task, Script Task, etc. Use generic tasks for simple, custom logic not covered by other types.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, a generic Task is executed using the default task handler. Input and output mappings can be defined using FEEL expressions. Variable scoping ensures only mapped variables are available. Error handling is supported, but advanced features (like service integration or user assignment) require specialized tasks.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A generic BPMN Task in TaktX is used for simple, custom logic. You can:

  • Define input and output mappings using FEEL expressions to control data flow.
  • Configure synchronous or asynchronous execution.
  • Set up error handling, retries, and compensation if needed.
  • Attach boundary events for error, escalation, or timer handling.
  • Monitor execution and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Use for lightweight, custom process steps not requiring external integration or user interaction.

 

Real-world BPMN Example for Generic Task

  • Use as a placeholder for documentation or modeling purposes.
  • Represents a generic activity with no specific behavior in TaktX.
  • Can be replaced with a more specific task type as the process evolves.
  • Monitor process flow and audit results via the TaktX client.

Example: Documentation Placeholder with Generic Task

 

This example shows a process where a Generic Task is used as a placeholder for a future activity. In TaktX, the Generic Task does nothing and the process continues directly without waiting. This is useful for documentation, modeling, or as a reminder to implement a specific activity later.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use generic tasks for simple, custom logic.
  • Switch to specialized tasks for advanced features.
  • Document the purpose and expected outcomes of each task.

Pitfalls:

  • Generic tasks lack advanced features (integration, assignment, etc.).
  • Unmapped variables will not be available.
  • Complex logic may be hard to maintain
